msContents.summary:
[p]Medical miscellany in Middle English, containing the [i]Booke of Ypocras[/i] and a collection of receipts (Leech-Books, II)[/p]
[p][b]Contents[/b][/p]
[p]1. ff. 1r-5v Lessons from the Four Gospels, beginning wanting[/p]
[p]f. 1r (red) Secundum lucam. In illo tempore missus est angelus (f. 1v) gabriel a deo in ciuitatem galilee cui nomen est nazareth ... f. 5v, line 9 (St. John, Ch. I) ... Et uidimus gloriam eius gloriam quasi unigeniti a patre Plenam gratie et ueritatis.
[p]2. ff. 5v-21r Charms and medical receipts in Latin and English[/p]
[p]f. 5v (red) Tak pouder of sandragon a nownce or a halfe of flex ... f. 21r ... For preuey euil that leuith with wommen ghif here to drinke mogwed with ale or soure wod. or wermod or the netle.[/p]
[p]3. ff. 21v-40r Pseudo-Hippocrates, [i]Booke of Ypocras[/i][/p]
[p]f. 21v (red) this is the bok that ypocras sent to the king his newuey ... f. 23v (end of introduction) fele thingis thow most lere. Now by ginne we a medecyn for the hed. Tak hulwort in eysel and do hit to his noseterlis ... f. 40r ... and that hit be sodyn ferst and kep hit for the nones.[/p]
[p]4. f. 40v Three charms.[/p]
[p]5. ff. 41r-66v Medical receipts in English[/p]
[p]f. 41r Ffor to make chardequince ... f. 66v (red) Nunc scripsi totum pro christo da michi potum. now haw y vryt alle ghyf me drynk of gode ale.[/p]
[p]6. ff. 67r-71v Blood-letting treatise in Latin and English[/p]
[p]f. 67r De dieta ex fleobotimacione in singulis mensibus anni. Januarius in the moneth of januer ... f. 71v ... and the xxix day December.[/p]
[p]7. ff. 72r-74v72 Latin charm against fever[/p]
[p]f. 72r In nomine patris et filii et spiritus sancti amen. Omnipotens sempiterne deus qui fecisti miraculum bono petro apostolo ... f. 74v ... et ita die in diem per nouem.[/p]
[p]8. ff. 75r-78v Prognostications according to the time of birth, extract (from February to May only)[/p]
[p]f. 75r ... fader of a noy mannes child sall he be cleped many noyis and blames ... f. 78v and in the reght fote he sall suffer maladies. men sall putt blames.[/p]

msItem.title: Medical miscellany in Middle English, containing the [i]Booke of Ypocras[/i] and a collection of receipts (Leech-Books, II)
msItem.filiation: Anglo Saxon letter forms in Moorat's catalogue description (such as contraction marks and Thorn and yogh symbols) have been replaced with Latin characters in this database description.

objectDesc.supportDesc: 1 volume78 ff. 16mo. 12 x 81 1/2 cm. On vellum. Modern vellum binding. The beginning and end are lost: the first and last leaves are damaged and the text badly rubbed. F. 20 is torn across and repaired. Written by several hands: the first 40 ff. in a clear gothic book hand, 16 lines to a page, mostly in a greenish ink, with capitals and paragraph marks in blue, headings in red. The introduction to the 'Book of Ypocras' (ff. 22v-23v) is written entirely in red. Ff. 41, 42 are in a less formal hand, 19 lines to a page: ff. 42-66 in a larger script, 13 lines to a page. A fourth hand, 15 lines to a page, is found on ff. 67-74. The last section (ff. 75-78) is written in a small semi-current informal hand, 19 lines to a page.

history.provenance: Attached is a letter to the unnamed owner of the MS. dated 13/3/1866, referring at length to its contents, etc., from the Very Rev. George William Kitchin [1827-1912], D.D., F.S.A. He dates it 1360-70, and considers it to be written in East Anglian dialect.
